title: Probabilistic circuit-breaker simulation and token-level load-shed dashboard
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a simulation-driven design and a Grafana dashboard to validate a probabilistic circuit-breaker admission policy that sheds requests at token granularity. The goal is to produce operational knobs (ramp curves, thresholds) that meet token-level latency SLOs without causing cache churn or unnecessary regional failovers.
background: We currently use threshold-based circuit breakers and regional failover. Thresholding spikes lead to cliff effects: sudden full rejection, cache invalidation, and higher downstream latency. For bursty token-heavy workloads (long context completions, reranking), graceful probabilistic shedding aligns better with user experience and reduces SLO violations. This ticket ties a simulator, telemetry queries, and a dashboard to iterate policy parameters against realistic traffic shapes.
acceptance_criteria: A simulator (python notebook + k8s job) that can replay traffic distributions and produce per-token admitted/rejected traces for a given policy
A Grafana dashboard with panels: token-admit rate, p50/p95/p99 token latency for admitted requests, shadow shed probability, and regional fallback rate
Baseline policy parameters (ramp function) that keep p99 token latency < 1.8x baseline under 3 synthetic burst profiles (short-chat, long-chat, reranker)
Recording rules/Prometheus queries for the new metrics and alerts for when admitted p99 diverges >20% from baseline
Runbook documenting when and how to change ramp parameters, and safe rollback steps
design_notes: Policy model: probabilistic drop prob p(q) where q is admission queue length. Use a three-segment piecewise ramp: flat 0 until q_start, linear ramp to p_max at q_crit, plateau p_max beyond q_crit.
We will expose two knobs per model-shard: q_start, q_crit, p_max. Also a global safety floor that forces 100% pass for golden traffic (health checks, control-plane).
Simulator will include: token-length sampling, interarrival distribution (Poisson and measured short-burst), and KV-cache hit modeling to capture cache churn cost of replays.
Decision: implement shedding at request admission (pre-compile) rather than mid-generation to avoid partial outputs and tail-kv inconsistencies.
Trade-off: pre-generation shedding loses progress in long running completions; mitigated by smaller q_start for long-context routes and per-route override.
We will avoid global abrupt fallbacks; instead escalate by region weight shifting (preferred) and only full cascade when admitted rate < 5% of baseline for >2m.
Security: simulator uses anonymized traces derived from synthetic profiles; no customer PII included.
telemetry_queries: PromQL: increase(rt_kv_cache_evictions_total[5m]) to estimate cache churn impact
PromQL: (sum(rate(rt_token_latency_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(rt_token_latency_seconds_count[5m]))) to get mean token latency by region/model
simulation_results: Simulation run #2026-02-22 short-chat burst (peak q=120): with q_start=40, q_crit=100, p_max=0.35 -> admitted p99 = 1.6x baseline, shed rate 18%, cache-evictions +4%
Simulation run #2026-02-26 long-chat burst (peak q=220): with q_start=30, q_crit=140, p_max=0.6 -> admitted p99 = 1.9x baseline (slightly over target), shed rate 32%, cache-evictions +12%

Simulation run #2026-03-01 reranker microbursts: single-shot long tokens, q_start=20, q_crit=80, p_max=0.45 -> admitted p99 = 1.5x baseline, shed rate 22%, observed fewer failovers when combined with optimistic region-weight shift
Key takeaway: p_max and q_crit must be routed per-route; single global policy overconstrains long-completions. We saw cache evictions correlate with aggressive p_max >0.5.
rollout_plan: Step 1 (canary): Deploy recording rules and dashboard to staging. Run simulator vs staging telemetry to validate PromQL semantics (48h).

Step 2 (shadow): Enable probabilistic policy in shadow admit path for 24h on <1% production traffic for model 'redwood-7b'. Log admits/rejects but don't enforce. Collect metrics and compare simulator predictions.

Step 3 (small canary): Enable enforcement for 5% of production traffic for 2h with conservative q_start/q_crit (lower p_max). Observe admitted p99 and cache eviction deltas. If p99>2x abort and rollback via feature-flag.

Step 4 (scaled ramp): Gradually increase to 50% over 24h with automated checks: no more than 10% increase in cache evictions and p99 <= 1.8x baseline. If breach, reduce to prior config and alert on-call.
Step 5 (global): After 72h stable, promote to all traffic per model and document final knobs in runtime-1.20 release notes.
open_questions: Should we include token-level grace for streaming responses (allow initial token credits before shedding)?
What telemetry latency is acceptable for the 'admit' metric pipeline? Current Prometheus scrape interval is 15s; simulator needs 5s resolution for burst alignment.
How to reconcile shed decisions with billing/usage attribution? Rejected requests currently still bill partial tokens in some paths; finance needs guidance.
Edge-case: interaction with KV-cache prefetch. If an admitted request triggers prefetch, we could see evictions before completion—how to surface this on dashboard?
